s1.syndrome_frame: A mass in the nasal cavity with a history of growth and bleeding, characterized by an exophytic and verrucous appearance
salient_findings: A 1-cm, nontender, exophytic, verrucous, skin-colored plaque on the right nasal vestibule
Papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium on histologic examination
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 30s
The mass has been growing for about 1 year
The lesion bleeds with minimal trauma
The patient does not smoke
The patient denies any medical history of chronic rhinosinusitis
The mass does not obstruct the patient's breathing
The physical examination revealed a 1-cm, nontender, exophytic, verrucous, skin-colored plaque on the right nasal vestibule
Histologic examination shows papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium
Mucin-containing goblet cells are present on histologic examination
Neither cytologic atypia nor atypical mitotic figures are present on histologic examination

per_call: Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma with Nasal Type

shortlist.label: Inverted Papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic examination shows papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium, consistent with inverted papilloma

shortlist.label: Verrucous Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Exophytic and verrucous appearance of the mass, along with histologic features of nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium, are consistent with verrucous carcinoma

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, squamous cell carcinoma cannot be ruled out due to the presence of a mass with a history of growth and bleeding

shortlist.label: Schneiderian Papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Mucin-containing goblet cells on histologic examination are consistent with schneiderian papilloma, a rare but plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Papillary Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Papillary architecture and nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium on histologic examination are consistent with papillary squamous cell carcinoma, a rare but possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and mucin-containing goblet cells, without cytologic atypia or atypical mitotic figures, is consistent with Schneiderian Papilloma.

rejected.label: Inverted Papilloma
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma typically shows inverted growth pattern, which is not described in the histologic examination.

rejected.label: Verrucous Carcinoma
rejected.why: Verrucous carcinoma typically shows cytologic atypia and has a more aggressive clinical course, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma typically shows cytologic atypia and atypical mitotic figures, which are not present in the histologic examination.

rejected.label: Papillary Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary squamous cell carcinoma is a rare variant of squamous cell carcinoma, and the histologic findings do not support this diagnosis.
